conventions.convention: Spacetime geometry uses η = diag(−1,1,1,1); Clifford and energy-momentum contractions use h = −η. Coordinates x⁰ = ct are in metres; energy-vector components and M = mc² are in joules, and s is in joules squared. Natural momentum coordinates divide energy components by ℏc.

The Hilbert pairing is first-variable-linear: (u,v)₁ = v†u. The coordinate contraction u†v is second-variable-linear and is its complex conjugate; modulus squares agree. These conventions assign no probability interpretation.

Gauge data have φ ∈ C¹(U;ℝ), A ∈ C¹(U;ℝ³), χ ∈ C²(U;ℝ), and ψ ∈ C¹(U;ℂᴺ), on nonempty open U ⊆ ℝ⁴. The lower potential is (−φ/c,A), Dₐ = ∂ₐ − iqAₐ/ℏ, and the gauge transformation is ψ ↦ exp(iqχ/ℏ)ψ, A ↦ A + dχ. The electron charge parameter is q = −e.

Finite Dyson dynamics assumes Countable Choice, d ≥ 1, T > 0, real dimensionless λ, positive ℏ, Hermitian H₀, and norm-continuous Hermitian V on [0,T]. The recursion places the latest-time factor on the left.

The Golden-rule weight is bounded, nonnegative Borel and continuous at E₀. The limit concerns the specified second-order integral coefficient P₂(T)/T, not an exact probability or exponential survival law.

Oscillator products act on the finite Hermite span. Time ordering puts X(t) first for t ≥ 0 and X(0) first for t < 0. Distributions pair bilinearly with complex Schwartz tests, and the frequency transform has positive sign exp(iνt), without 2π normalization. Distributional convergence means convergence against every Schwartz test.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the geometric/algebraic metric distinction, SI energy and natural-coordinate conversions, dimensionless coupling, gauge conventions, and first-variable-linear Hilbert pairing for constructed/formal examples; makes no empirical or interacting-continuum existence claim.

Under its Countable Choice and finite Hermitian norm-continuous dynamics hypotheses, the Dyson series converges in operator norm, solves the evolution equation uniquely, is unitary, and has remainder at most exp(z)z^(N+1)/(N+1)!. Exact unitarity gives the diagonal identity and first two coefficient identities. The two-level model separates exact and first-order squares and excludes positive-rate exponential survival; occupation truncation has commutator I − (N+1)|N⟩⟨N|.

Under Countable Choice and positive oscillator parameters, C_F(t) = exp(−iω|t|)/(2ω), (∂ₜ²+ω²)C_F = −iδ₀, and (∂ₜ²+ω²)G_R = δ₀. The positive-sign transform of the damped correlator has the displayed opposite pole prescriptions and their Schwartz-distribution boundary limit. C_F is nonzero at negative times whereas G_R vanishes there.

Under Countable Choice, K_T has integral 2π, normalized tail mass at most 4/(πTr), and bounded Borel tests continuous at zero satisfy the error bound ω_f(r) + 8‖f‖∞/(πTr). For the stated bounded nonnegative weight continuous at E₀, P₂(T) is finite and P₂(T)/T tends to 2πλ²w(E₀)/ℏ.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact countable-choice assumption retained by dynamics, oscillator, Fourier, integral-limit results and examples.
Unique Volterra solution, norm-Dyson convergence and unitarity for norm-continuous bounded self-adjoint generators on compact intervals.
Power-series definition of the exponential used in oscillator phase and damped-transform calculations.
Euler formula, unit modulus of real-frequency phases, and the Golden-kernel sine expression.
Negative-sign 2π-normalized integral Fourier transform and conversion to the positive-sign angular-frequency transform.
Affine substitutions in the Golden-kernel normalization and energy-coefficient integral, under Countable Choice and Borel measurability.
L² norm preservation giving the total Golden-kernel mass.
Identification of the interval indicator's integral transform with its L² Fourier transform almost everywhere.
Smooth test functions with bounded polynomially weighted derivatives in the oscillator distribution argument.
Complex L² completeness and its first-variable-linear integral pairing, used to extend oscillator phase isometries.
Position multiplication on Hermite vectors and invariance of the finite Hermite span.
Scaled complete orthonormal oscillator family, self-adjoint Hamiltonian, oscillator length and exact eigenvalues.
Differentiation and integration of the damped exponential kernels.
Interchange of absolutely integrable time-frequency integrals identifying the ordinary damped transform with the dual distribution action.
Preservation and continuity of the Schwartz test space under Fourier transformation in the boundary-limit argument.

concerns.concern: The Statement and proof step 3.1 write '2 Im T₂ = T₁†T₁' without defining the imaginary part of a matrix. The derivation requires Im_H A = (A − A†)/(2i), rather than entrywise imaginary part. For constant V = [[1,i],[-i,1]], H₀ = 0 and numerical ℏ = T = 1, T₁ = −V and T₂ = iV²/2; entrywise 2 Im T₂ lacks the nonzero imaginary off-diagonal entries of V². The physical consumer pthm-qft-example-regulated-probability-control explicitly supplies the correct Hermitian imaginary-part definition. The supplier should make the same convention explicit.

seams_checked.note: Observable types preserve the SI/natural-unit and finite-matrix conventions. Regulated probability control uses the exact finite Dyson hypotheses and remainder, retains Countable Choice, and separately adopts preparation, evolution and Born assumptions. It explicitly defines the Hermitian imaginary part for the coefficient identity.

The page and its phase-space, spin-trace, annihilation, scalar-coefficient and Pauli-square interfaces preserve h = −η, joule-valued energy coordinates, ℏc conversion, dimensionless coupling and SI gauge units. Formal coefficients and differential identities are not promoted to exact continuum or empirical claims.

Cutoff-integral and soft-current statements preserve inverse-length versus energy coordinates, h contractions and dimensionless g. The coherent construction explicitly chooses the second-variable-linear pairing, compatible with the supplier's conjugation conversion, and retains its mathematical rather than empirical scope.

The Penning lemma's declared item dependency and L1 accurately quote M = mc² and use m = M/c² only for the mass-energy conversion. Dynamics and stable-mode spectral hypotheses are supplied locally. The page describes this reliance faithfully, although its frontmatter contains no explicit requires list.
